stem: iv. Write the IUPAC name of the compound shown in the figure.

Draw structures of following compounds.

i. 2,5-Diethylphenol
ii. Prop-2-en-1-ol
iii. 2-methoxypropane
iv. Phenylmethanol
solution:
i. **2,5-Diethylphenol** — a benzene ring carrying \(\mathrm{-OH}\) at C-1 and an ethyl group \(\mathrm{(-C_2H_5)}\) at each of C-2 and C-5:

\(\mathrm{2,5\text{-}(C_2H_5)_2\text{-}C_6H_3\text{-}OH}\)

ii. **Prop-2-en-1-ol** — \(\mathrm{H_2C{=}CH-CH_2-OH}\) (the \(\mathrm{-OH}\) is on C-1 and the double bond between C-2 and C-3).

iii. **2-methoxypropane** — \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(O-CH_3)-CH_3}\), i.e. a methoxy group on the middle carbon of propane.

iv. **Phenylmethanol** — \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2-OH}\), a benzene ring bearing a \(\mathrm{-CH_2-OH}\) group.

stem:
Predict the products for the following reaction.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CHO}\) (A)

i. with \(\mathrm{H_2/Ni}\)

ii. with (i) \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\) (ii) \(\mathrm{H_3O^{\oplus}}\)
solution:
The substrate (A) contains an isolated \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\) and an aldehyde group. \(\mathrm{H_2/Ni}\) can reduce both these functional groups while \(\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\) can reduce only \(\mathrm{-CHO}\) of the two. Hence

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CHO} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2/Ni}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CHO} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ H_3O^{\oplus}}]{\mathrm{(i)\ LiAlH_4}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH-CH_2-CH_2-OH}\)

stem: The boiling points of n-butyl alcohol, isobutyl alcohol, sec-butyl alcohol and tert-butyl alcohol are \(118^\circ\mathrm{C}\), \(108^\circ\mathrm{C}\), \(99.5^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and \(83^\circ\mathrm{C}\) respectively. Explain.
solution: As branching increases intermolecular van der Waal's force become weaker and the boiling point decreases. Therefore n-butyl alcohol has highest boiling point \(118^\circ\mathrm{C}\) and tert-butyl alcohol has lowest boiling point \(83^\circ\mathrm{C}\). Isobutyl alcohol is a primary alcohol and hence its boiling point is higher than that of sec-butyl alcohol.

stem: The solubility of o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol is \(0.2\ \mathrm{g}\) and \(1.7\ \mathrm{g}/100\ \mathrm{g}\) of \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) respectively. Explain the difference.
solution:
In o-nitrophenol the \(\mathrm{-OH}\) and \(\mathrm{-NO_2}\) groups are on adjacent carbons, so the phenolic hydrogen is locked up in an **intramolecular** hydrogen bond with an oxygen of the nitro group. In p-nitrophenol the two groups are far apart, so no such intramolecular bond is possible and the \(\mathrm{-OH}\) is free to form **intermolecular** hydrogen bonds with water.

p-Nitrophenol has strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding with solvent water. On the other hand, o-nitrophenol has strong intramolecular hydrogen bonding and therefore the intermolecular attraction towards solvent water is weak. The stronger the intermolecular attraction between solute and solvent, higher is the solubility. Hence p-nitrophenol has higher solubility in water than that of o-nitrophenol.

stem:
Arrange the following compounds in decreasing order of acid strength and justify.

i. \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-OH}\)
ii. \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH}\)
iii. \(\mathrm{C_6H_5-OH}\)
iv. \(\mathrm{p\text{-}NO_2-C_6H_4-OH}\)
solution:
Compounds (iii) and (iv) are phenols and therefore are more acidic than the alcohols (i) and (ii). The acidic strengths of compounds depend upon stabilization of the corresponding conjugate bases. Hence let us compare electronic effects in the conjugate bases of these compounds :

**Alcohols :** \(\mathrm{CH_3 \rightarrow CH_2 \rightarrow O^{\ominus}}\) (conjugate base of (i)) and \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_3C \rightarrow O^{\ominus}}\) (conjugate base of (ii)).

The conjugate base of the alcohol (i) is destabilized by \(+\mathrm{I}\) effect of one alkyl group, whereas conjugate base of the alcohol (ii) is destabilized by \(+\mathrm{I}\) effect of three alkyl groups. Hence (ii) is weaker acid than (i).

**Phenols :** The conjugate base of p-nitrophenol (iv) is better resonance stabilized due to six resonance structures compared to the five resonance structures of conjugate base of phenol (iii). The resonance structure VI has \(-\)ve charge on only electronegative oxygens. Hence the phenol (iv) is stronger acid than (iii).

Thus the decreasing order of acid strength is \((\mathrm{iv}) > (\mathrm{iii}) > (\mathrm{i}) > (\mathrm{ii})\).

stem: Write the reaction showing major and minor products formed on heating butan-2-ol with concentrated sulfuric acid.
solution:
In the reaction described butan-2-ol undergoes dehydration to give but-2-ene (major) and but-1-ene (minor) in accordance with Saytzeff rule.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3} \xrightarrow[-\mathrm{H_2O},\ \Delta]{\text{Conc. } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH-CH_3}\) (But-2-ene, major)

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_3} \xrightarrow[-\mathrm{H_2O},\ \Delta]{\text{Conc. } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathrm{CH_2{=}CH-CH_2-CH_3}\) (But-1-ene, minor)

stem: Write and explain reactions to convert propan-1-ol into propan-2-ol.
solution:
The dehydration of propan-1-ol to propene is the first step. Markownikoff hydration of propene is the second step to get the product propan-2-ol. This is brought about by reaction with concentrated \(\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\) followed by hydrolysis.

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-OH} \xrightarrow[623\ \mathrm{K}]{\mathrm{Al_2O_3}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH_2}\) (Propene)

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{(ii)\ H_2O}]{\text{(i) Con. } \mathrm{H_2SO_4}} \mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3}\) (Propan-2-ol)

stem: An organic compound gives hydrogen on reaction with sodium metal. It forms an aldehyde having molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O}\) on oxidation with pyridinium chlorochromate. Name the compounds and give equations of these reactions.
solution:
The given molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_2H_4O}\) of aldehyde is written as \(\mathrm{CH_3-CHO}\). Hence the formula of alcohol from which this is obtained by oxidation must be \(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-OH}\). The two reactions can, therefore, be represented as follows.

\(2\,\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-OH} \xrightarrow{2\mathrm{Na}} 2\,\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2O^{\ominus}Na^{\oplus}} + \mathrm{H_2}\uparrow\)

(Ethyl alcohol) \(\longrightarrow\) (Sodium ethoxide)

\(\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-OH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{PCC}]{[\mathrm{O}]} \mathrm{CH_3-CHO} + \mathrm{H_2O}\)

(Ethyl alcohol) \(\longrightarrow\) (Acetaldehyde)

stem:
Ethyl isopropyl ether does not form on reaction of sodium ethoxide and isopropyl chloride.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5-ONa} + \mathrm{Cl-CH(CH_3)-CH_3} \nrightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_5-O-CH(CH_3)-CH_3}\)

i. What would be the main product of this reaction ?

ii. Write another reaction suitable for the preparation of ethyl isopropyl ether.
solution:
i. Isopropyl chloride is a secondary chloride. On treating with sodium ethoxide it gives elimination reaction to form propene as the main product.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5-ONa} + \mathrm{Cl-CH(CH_3)-CH_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{CH_3-CH{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{C_2H_5OH} + \mathrm{NaCl}\)

(Sodium ethoxide) + (isopropyl chloride) \(\longrightarrow\) (Propene) + (Ethyl alcohol)

ii. Ethyl isopropyl ether can be prepared by using ethyl chloride (\(1^\circ\) chloride) as substrate.

\(\mathrm{C_2H_5-Cl} + \mathrm{Na^{\oplus}O^{\ominus}-CH(CH_3)-CH_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{C_2H_5-O-CH(CH_3)-CH_3} + \mathrm{NaCl}\)

(Ethyl chloride) + (Sodium isopropoxide) \(\longrightarrow\) (ethyl isopropyl ether)
